title: Environmental Chemistry: Air and Water Pollution and Acid Rain

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why some rivers in Nigeria are polluted or why the air sometimes feels heavy? Let's explore the chemistry behind these environmental issues.

blocks.markdown: Environmental chemistry focuses on the chemical processes occurring in the environment and their impacts. In this lesson, we will discuss air and water pollution, and the formation of acid rain.

blocks.title: Air Pollutants
blocks.text: Air pollutants are substances in the air that can cause harm to humans and the environment. Common examples include carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen oxides.

blocks.markdown: In Nigeria, common sources of air pollutants include vehicle emissions, industrial discharges, and burning of fossil fuels. These pollutants can lead to health issues and environmental damage.

Acid rain is a significant environmental problem caused by air pollution. It forms when sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) react with water vapor in the atmosphere to form sulfuric and nitric acids. These acids then fall to the ground as precipitation.

blocks.title: Formation of Acid Rain
blocks.prompt: Explain how acid rain forms from sulfur dioxide.

steps.text: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is released into the atmosphere from burning fossil fuels.
SO₂ reacts with water vapor in the air to form sulfurous acid (H₂SO₃).
Further oxidation of sulfurous acid forms sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), which then mixes with rainwater.

blocks.answer: Acid rain forms when sulfur dioxide reacts with water vapor to form sulfuric acid, which falls as precipitation.

blocks.title: Reducing Pollution
blocks.text: One method to reduce air pollution is using catalytic converters in vehicles to reduce emissions of harmful gases.

points: Common air pollutants include carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen oxides.

Reducing pollution can involve using cleaner technologies and practices.
